facts.fact: The Interior ministry's ID4Africa deck shows the automated national civil-status register holding three databases, births, deaths and marriages, with entry, control and update (saisie, contrôle et MAJ) at commune level; it gives no date for the state described, so the presentation date is used.
facts.system: Registre National automatisé de l'état civil

facts.fact: The deck's system architecture shows 1,541 commune databases (C1 to C1541) where entry, control and update are done, linked over the ministry's network to 48 wilaya databases for error correction and to a national database at the ministry; elsewhere the deck speaks of 'the 1541 communes'. No date is given, so the presentation date is used.
facts.system: Registre National automatisé de l'état civil

facts.fact: The automated national civil-status register, instituted by Law 14-08 of 9 August 2014, is presented by the Interior ministry's director general of modernisation as the ministry's own system, with the national database held at ministry (MICLAT) level; the presentation date is used.
facts.system: Registre National automatisé de l'état civil

systems.system: Registre National automatisé de l'état civil
systems.country_label: Registre National automatisé de l'état civil; Registre National informatisé de l'Etat Civil
systems.owner: Ministère de l'Intérieur, des Collectivités Locales et de l'Aménagement du Territoire (MICLAT)
systems.tiers: 1,541 commune databases (entry, control and update), 48 wilaya databases (error correction), one national database at the ministry, over the ministry's network; acts of birth, marriage and death issued in under a minute from any commune or annex
102 million acts scanned and keyed: 68.65 million births, 17.70 million deaths, 15.64 million marriages

systems.system: Interconnexion des secteurs au Registre National de l'Etat Civil
systems.tiers: Ministries and institutions that ask for civil-status documents consult the national register directly
18-character number generated automatically from civil-status data on the birth act; described as a key component of the national civil-status register
Enrolment decentralised to communes; card applications read and updated by communes over the intranet
Launched January 2012; enrolment sites in 541 daïras, 13 administrative circumscriptions and 163 consular services, then decentralised to the 1,541 communes
Reference platform for all identity-linked services, tied by the NIN to civil status, CNIBE, passport and driving licence

note: No `made` fact: the deck places entry, control and update at commune level feeding a national database, but does not say the entry is made at registration.
